title: Timezone-aware release window planner and comms microprotocol
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact working planner for releases that span multiple regions. It combines a timezone-aware calendar, a short preflight checklist focused on cross-region risk, and a lightweight communications microprotocol for fast, unambiguous ops during rollout. Aim is to reduce cognitive load for on-call and deployment owners when coordinating across NA/EU/APAC.

Scope:
- Applies to all production deployments that will shift traffic or model routing across regions
- Intended for releases that have staged traffic (canary -> ramp -> global) and a 48h post-release monitoring window
- Not a full runbook for catastrophic incidents (see incident-runbook); this is an operations/coordination tool

Quick summary of novel bits (what's different here):
- Timezone-prescriptive windows (UTC-first templates plus conversions for target on-call regions)
- Microprotocol: 4-line message templates for Slack + Pager duty tags to avoid ambiguous updates
- Acceptance-signal definitions that are numeric (SLOs) and logical (no regression in error-types)

Preflight checklist (owner: release lead)
- Confirm canary image hash and Git tag: git rev-parse --short HEAD => include in release note
- Verify migration/backwards-compat flags are toggled in feature-flag console (FF-Tier-1)
- Capacity smoke: validate baseline load test RPS vs expected traffic spike and reserve 20% headroom
- Telemetry: alert runbooks linked, dashboards pinned (latency, 5xx rate, queue depth by region, KV cache hit-rate)
- Rollback hooks present: k8s rollback command noted, and SQL migrations are reversible (if any)
- On-call coverage: at least one SRE in region during canary + one cross-region release buddy
- Release artifacts published: changelog draft, dependency matrix, and a short customer-impact blurb

Timezone release calendar (template)
- All times in UTC first, then local conversions (examples for this release):
  - Canary start: 2026-04-07 14:00 UTC (NA morning: 07:00 PT, EU afternoon: 15:00 CET, APAC overnight: 23:00 JST)
  - Canary observe window: 30 minutes steady-state + 5m sampling every 5m = total 30m
  - Canary ramp to 10%: 2026-04-07 14:30 UTC
  - Canary to 50%: 2026-04-07 15:30 UTC (if all green)
  - Full rollout begin: 2026-04-07 17:00 UTC
  - Post-rollout watch: 48h focusing first 6h intensive watch (alert triage cadence 10m)

Why UTC-first?
- UTC anchors reduce conversion mistakes. Local conversions are listed in the calendar for convenience; escalation always uses UTC timestamps.

Canary plan (owner: service owner)
- Step 0: Baseline capture (T-15m): snapshot 10m rolling latency percentiles, 5xx counts, queue depth
- Step 1: Deploy canary to a single AZ (hash XXX) at Canary start
- Step 2: Observe 30m. Acceptance signals: p95 latency within +10% of baseline, no spike in model-serving 500s, KV cache hit-rate within -5%
- Step 3: If acceptance signals OK, bump to 10% traffic over 5m increments, observe 20m at each increment
- Step 4: If stable, escalate to 50% for 1h; then gating decision to global ramp
- Abort criteria (any one): sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive 1m windows OR p95 latency > +40% for 5m OR error type shift (new error class)

Communication microprotocol (owner: release comms lead)
- Channel structure: #releases (primary), #releases-ops (private), PagerDuty escalation (PO-sre-oncall)
- Message taxonomy: STATUS | UTC_TS | SCOPE | SHORT-BODY | ACTION-TAG
  - STATUS = START|UPDATE|HOLD|ABORT|COMPLETE
  - UTC_TS = e.g. 2026-04-07T14:00Z
  - SCOPE = canary|10pct|50pct|global
  - ACTION-TAG = @oncall @db-team (use existing PD/Slack mappings)
- Templates (copy-paste friendly):
  - START: START | 2026-04-07T14:00Z | canary | Deploying canary image githash XXX to eu-west-1 | @oncall
  - UPDATE: UPDATE | 2026-04-07T14:20Z | canary | Observed latency p95 +2% vs baseline; 5xx stable; continuing | @oncall
  - ABORT: ABORT | 2026-04-07T14:35Z | canary | 5xx rate 1.2% sustained -> rolling back to previous stable | @oncall @eng-release-engineering
  - COMPLETE: COMPLETE | 2026-04-07T17:00Z | global | Full rollout complete; post-watch next 48h | @eng-release-engineering
- Escalation ladder: 1) release lead -> 2) SRE oncall -> 3) Eng manager -> 4) CTO (only for business-impacting rollbacks)

Operational quick commands (for rapid rollback or safe checkpoints)
- k8s rollback quick: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=REV
- disable route (fast fallback): curl -X POST $ROUTER_ADMIN/route/fallback?service=model-serving
- force drain a canary node: ./ops/drain-node.sh <node-id> --release-safe

Acceptance signals (numeric + human)
- Numeric (automated):
  - p95 latency <= baseline * 1.10
  - 5xx rate <= 0.5% average over 5m windows
  - KV cache-hit >= baseline -5%
- Human checks (explicit):
  - No unexplained errors in Sentry or error tracer dashboards
  - Model output regression: quick eval set sampled (10 prompts) run through canary returns >= 95% similarity in regen test (automated eval job ID attached)

Rollout calendar (compact)
- 2026-04-07T13:45Z: Release lead posts START message and baseline snapshot
- 2026-04-07T14:00Z: Canary deploy begins (eu-west-1)
- 2026-04-07T14:30Z: Ramp to 10% if green
- 2026-04-07T15:30Z: Ramp to 50% if green
- 2026-04-07T17:00Z: Global start
- 2026-04-09T17:00Z: End of 48h watch window and postmortem draft due if issues

Draft release notes (first-pass):
- Title: model-serving: dynamic-kv-cache + attention-opt kernel (v2.11.0)
- Highlights:
  - Reduced 99th percentile CPU bursts by ~15% on heavy prompt loads (internal sim)
  - Enabled hot-KV-prefetch for short-context workloads (default off, opt-in via FF)
  - Performance tuning for attention kernels on A100x2 (improves p95 latency)
- User-impact blurb:
  - No API contract changes. Some customers may observe lower latency for short prompt patterns. If you depend on exact tokenization timing, please validate in staging.
- Migration notes:
  - No DB migrations. Rolling restart only. Feature flags allow immediate rollback of hot-KV-prefetch.
- Known issues:
  - Observed small variance in cache-hit on cold starts for the first 10 minutes in small AZs. Monitoring alert created (ALERT-5587).

Draft post-release checklist (first 6h):
- Confirm ingestion pipelines healthy and retraces showing no spike in failure rate
- Verify canary node utilization not increasing queue depth beyond baseline + 10%
- Confirm evictions count stable in telemetry and model-serving VM memory not thrashing
- Remind support to use the release notes blurb when triaging customer tickets

Retrospective prompts (for postmortem):
- Did the timezone windows minimize cognitive handoffs? Any missed conversions?
- Were comms messages consistently using the microprotocol taxonomy?
- Any gaps in automation that increased manual approval frequency?

Appendix: Quick timezone cheatsheet (for this release)
- 2026-04-07T14:00Z = 2026-04-07 07:00 PT / 10:00 ET / 15:00 CET / 23:00 JST
- Use /convert-time in #releases-bot to check alternate locations; always include UTC in messages

Short TODOs before sign-off:
- [ ] Attach automated regression eval job ID and link the dataset used to the PR
- [ ] Confirm DB-free rollout path for feature flag in case of rollback
- [ ] Assign post-release note owner for 48h watch window

Notes to self (rough):
- If APAC coverage is only default overnight, keep canary small to avoid waking too many folks; prefer EU-first canary for NA-moving-hours releases
- Consider adding a tiny synthetic traffic generator as a canary probe to exercise worst-case token lengths

End of doc.
